description.description: A series of four screenshots of a smartphone displaying a PDF document titled 'Patrolling/Commuting' from a Proton Drive link. The document provides instructions for community 'patrols' monitoring ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) activity. It includes guidelines for mobile and foot patrols, a list of items to bring (like PPE and chargers) and not to bring (like weapons or children), information on using whistles as an alert system, tips for identifying 'abductor' vehicles, and protocols for communicating with dispatchers and documenting interactions while staying safe. The document repeatedly refers to ICE agents as 'abductors' or 'Federal Agents.'
description.ocrText: 10:57 Signal . Proton Drive: Cloud Storage Secure files & photos storage Get In-App Purchases X Patrol ... te.pdf < 1 of 1 > 2 Patrolling/Commuting . Because of their speed, Mobile Patrols and Stationed Monitors are the most useful roles right now and have contributed to stopping abductions that happen fast. Try it out! . Abductors are circling back to a lot to the places that they want to be, so a combination of Mobile Patrol and Stationary Monitoring is extra-helpful. . Pick an area and dedicate yourself to it. You will be best able to respond in neighborhoods and on streets that you know and are familiar with. . Not everyone needs to respond to everything that happens everywhere. Consider staying put if it seems like others are responding. Even when there are big raid mobilizations it does not mean that other teams aren't operating in other places. . If in doubt, ask dispatch on the call or in the chat if you're needed vs doing your own thing. . It can be helpful to review this marshall/deescalation training to help keep yourself grounded and safe while on patrols. . It can also be helpful to review Monarca training for rapid response if you've not had any formal trainings yet or if it's been awhile. . Download Ready Now and add Kevin Riach, 612-203-8555 attorney to the legal notification field. He is the primary contact for detained observers. . If you are commuting in a car, we strongly advise that you make sure your license and registration are current, all of your lights are working and your vehicle is in safe operating condition before heading out. Commuters have been pulled over for these things as well as for traffic violations. A. Mobile Patrol 1. Join the group call (push the camera button at the top or bottom of the chat) and stay on mute when not communicating. 2. Being on the call is a hands-free way to communicate that keeps chat clear. 3. Download the READY NOW app to alert your emergency contacts in the case of a detainment. 4. When documenting, do it with the phone locked if there's any risk they might grab the phone. 5. You should not be patrolling and dispatching at the same time - this is not safe! 6. Do not bring pets, children, or vulnerable people. 7. If something upsetting happens, it's okay to ask for aftercare and support! That's what we're here for as a community. . Lay on your horn when you confirm abductor presence to warn others and to chase them off drive.proton.me ... • Throwaway jacket (in case of tear gas) • Warm clothing/gloves/hats/hand warmers • Face mask/bandana/face covering, etc. • Sunglasses or goggles • Water (a lot of it) • Cheap towels • Phone chargers and power banks • Wired earbuds • Ear protection for whistle fatigue • Extra umbrellas • Disposable PPE • Basic first-aid supplies • Pepper spray PPE and treatment supplies including a sport tip water bottle (see chemical weapons section for more information) • Food/water • Notebook, pen Everything you carry is for comforting, protecting, or stabilizing someone in distress. Items/Things/People To Not Bring or Considerations: • Weapons (even a pocket knife or utility knife) • Valuables • Pets, children or vulnerable/high risk people • Alcohol C. Foot Patrol 1. Foot patrols are a little harder to see moving vehicles with, but can still be great for hyperlocal observation, exercise, and being in the right place at the right time. 2. Have a cheap pair of binoculars or a monocular with you for spotting things easily at a distance. 3. If possible, go in pairs, especially at night. Try to be covert - hide whistles but keep them accessible - you're just going for a walk around the neighborhood. If other neighbors seem concerned, give a friendly wave. 3. Information for all patrol types A. Patrol Decision Tree Unverified - Patrol/Daily Chat Patrol See something suspicious ! Tip ! Information from a different chat or community drive.proton.me ... • Night/Evening operations/patrols • Losing contact with partner/phone • Exposing name and address via plate scanners • Local Police Department arrives to support ICE • ICE pointing firearms at unarmed civilians In Red, always have a partner, you stay visible, avoid isolation, contact dispatch, get ready for a READY NOW alert on your phone, and rely on your partner. WHISTLES! INSTANT ALERT SYSTEM SIMPLE. EFFECTIVE. FASTER THAN SOCIAL MEDIA TOGETHER. WE KEEP OUR COMMUNITY SAFE C. Whistles Whistle graphic: congrats you're now whistle trained! Find more whistle information for MN here: https://linktr.ee/mspwhistles HOW WHISTLES WORK WEAR A WHISTLE IF YOU SPOT ICE, BLOW YOUR WHISTLE WHEN YOU HEAR A WHISTLE, EITHER: • GET TO SAFETY • FOLLOW THE SOUND, FORM A CROWD, STAY LOUD WHISTLE CODE #1: ICE NEARBY IF ICE IS DRIVING OR LURKING: BLOW IN SHORT BLASTS PRE--PRE--PRE--PRE WHISTLE CODE #2: ABDUCTION IF ICE IS ABDUCTING SOMEONE: BLOW CONTINUOUSLY PREEEEEEE-PREEEEEEE D. Identifying Abductors/Vehicles Look for some combination of these potential factors that make it more likely: . Occupants: . People inside are mostly in pairs (though sometimes 1, sometimes 3+) . Driver and passenger wearing neck gaiters or buffs that they pull up over their faces to mask their identities . Wearing vests or have tactical gear . ICE agents in or out of their vehicle drive.proton.me ... abducted by Federal Agents. • Do not post anything from a chat to social media, only post what you have seen yourself. • Do not go live on social media: live cannot be controlled, remember that - anything that happened is now public and can be used against you or any other people responding/commuting/observing. • When you can, try to remain as calm as possible. Steady your hands. • Follow up with the family or friend contacts to try to let them know what happened. • If there are loved ones or children left behind when the person was abducted, check in with them and do what you can to help them connect with resources and support. See some support numbers here under "Immigrant Legal Know Your Rights, Support after an Abduction, and Family Planning" • MN Emergency Legal Guide During/After an ICE Arrest - Gua de Emergencia Legal durante/tras una Detencin por ICE - Minnesota • This is a Google document. Be sure you are not signed into Google, or signed into Google Docs on a mobile device when clicking this link. • Inform the Monarca line with your documentation when you have time. 612-441-2881. • Report unlawful ICE conduct or racial profiling, warrantless stops, or detention by federal law enforcement to the ACLU on this page H. Communicating with Dispatchers • Be sure to add your emoji and join the call in your RR group before you head out • Verbally dictate plates to be checked to the dispatchers • Stay on mute when you're not talking • Participate in each role call if you can safely • Be sure to update your username and inform dispatch when you are ending a shift I. ICE Tactics/Police Abductor intimidation of Responders: • Responders commuting behind abductors will have sometimes find that they have led them to their own homes. If this happens you can drive to a place you feel comfortable with that is public and has cameras. • To report ICE rights violations, or police harassment to the ACLU: https://www.aclu-mn.org/ice-feds-form/ ICE box-ins: • Some responders have been deliberately boxed in by agent vehicles, surrounded, and trapped by abductors. • Abductors may yell and hit the window of the car and some have waved and pointed guns. • If you are pulled over, ensure that your doors are locked and your windows are rolled all drive.proton.me ...
